title: Clinical AI agents require oversight beyond answer accuracy
zh_title: 临床AI智能体需超越答案准确性的监督
summary: 观点文章提出临床 AI 智能体的安全监督应考察目标、叙事、工具、不确定性与停止条件。
key_points: 智能体跨步骤执行任务改变安全问题的性质
仅校验答案正确性不足以覆盖风险
建议在进入临床工作流前实施多维监督
reason: 提出智能体监督框架，具讨论价值但无实证数据，属观点类上限档
abstract: Clinical AI agents can carry tasks across steps. This changes the safety problem. The question is not only whether an AI system gives a correct response, but what working narrative it carries into action. A wrong narrative can move through tools, tasks, and care. Clinical oversight should examine the agent’s goal, narrative, tools, uncertainty, and stopping conditions before it enters workflow.
zh_abstract: 临床AI智能体可以跨步骤执行任务。这改变了安全问题。问题不仅在于AI系统是否给出正确回应，还在于它把什么样的工作叙事带入行动。错误的叙事可能通过工具、任务和诊疗流程传播。临床监督应在智能体进入工作流程之前，审查其目标、叙事、工具、不确定性和停止条件。

title: Risk governance for generative AI mental health support: a multi-turn safety architecture
zh_title: 生成式AI心理健康支持的风险治理架构
summary: npj Digital Medicine提出模型外置的多轮风险治理架构，在合成对话中提升风险识别与升级回应率。
key_points: 结合情境风险检测、推理校验与协议化回应生成
合成对话中敏感度0.92、特异度0.85
临床医生偏好的升级回应提升25.6–59.2个百分点
reason: 同行评审新方法且有置信区间，但仅合成对话评估、无真实临床结局，属值得一看档
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health support despite lacking mechanisms to safely govern evolving risk. Existing safety approaches primarily detect risk but rarely shape how models respond as conversational risk unfolds. We developed a portable, model-external safety governance architecture that combines contextual risk detection, reasoning-based verification, and protocol-guided response generation for multi-turn mental health interactions. Using synthetic conversations grounded in real-world mental health narratives, the architecture’s performance was assessed with GPT-5-chat and Qwen3.5-27B, increasing clinician-preferred escalation responses by 25.6–59.2 pp, while achieving high risk detection performance (specificity: 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity: 0.92 (95%CI: 0.89;0.95)). Performance remained stable across conversation length and across models (proprietary and open-source), with preliminary evidence showing that rapport and connection were preserved. These findings demonstrate that clinically-grounded governance can extend beyond risk detection to improve how LLMs manage evolving mental health risk, providing a framework for scalable safety governance.
zh_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地用于心理健康支持，尽管其缺乏对不断演变的风险进行安全治理的机制。现有安全方法主要检测风险，但很少在对话风险展开时塑造模型的回应方式。我们开发了一种可移植的模型外部安全治理架构，针对多轮心理健康交互，结合了情境风险检测、基于推理的验证和协议引导的回应生成。使用以真实世界心理健康叙事为基础的合成对话，采用GPT-5-chat和Qwen3.5-27B评估该架构的性能，使临床医生偏好的升级回应增加了25.6–59.2个百分点（pp），同时实现高水平的风险检测性能（特异度：0.85（95%CI：0.78；0.91），灵敏度：0.92（95%CI：0.89；0.95））。性能在对话长度以及不同模型（专有和开源）之间保持稳定，初步证据显示融洽关系和联结感得以保留。这些发现表明，以临床为基础的治理可以超越风险检测，改善LLMs管理不断演变的心理健康风险的方式，为可扩展的安全治理提供框架。

title: MedDx, a training-free AI phenotyping model, identifies alcohol use disorder in cirrhosis with hepatologist-level agreement
zh_title: MedDx：免训练模型从病历识别肝硬化患者酒精使用障碍
summary: 基于印第安纳肝硬化注册库485例病历，开源免训练模型MedDx识别酒精使用障碍，与病历复核金标准及肝病专家一致性高。
key_points: 三分类与金标准κ 0.92，诊断码仅0.67
与两位肝病专家κ 0.85/0.82，专家间0.87
加权后敏感度98%、特异度94%
reason: 预印本、单注册库回顾性，样本485例，有医师对照但无外部验证，属值得一看档
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is often under-documented in patients with cirrhosis, which delays treatment. Expert chart review of clinical notes can identify under-documented AUD, but is not scalable. We propose MedDx, an open-weight, training-free, and engine-agnostic language model, to phenotype AUD using clinical notes in patients with cirrhosis. We benchmarked MedDx on a 485-patient study cohort sampled from the 14,406-patient Indiana Cirrhosis Registry, using a chart-review-based reference as ground truth. MedDx agreed with the ground truth at three-class Cohen's {kappa} 0.92, against 0.67 for the AUD diagnosis code. It agreed with one hepatologist at 0.85 on all 485 charts and with a second at 0.82 on 186 charts, on which the two hepatologists agreed at 0.87. Weighted to the registry, its sensitivity was 98% and specificity 94%, against 63% and 96% for the AUD diagnosis code, and 61% of an estimated 6,223 patients with AUD had no AUD diagnosis by the first cirrhosis diagnosis. MedDx is openly available as an off-the-shelf, equitable, and auditable tool to identify AUD.
zh_abstract: 酒精使用障碍（AUD）在肝硬化患者中常记录不足，这会延误治疗。由专家对临床记录进行病历审查可识别记录不足的AUD，但不可扩展。我们提出MedDx，一种开放权重、无需训练且与引擎无关的语言模型，用于利用肝硬化患者的临床记录对AUD进行表型识别。我们在从14,406例患者的印第安纳肝硬化登记（Indiana Cirrhosis Registry）中抽取的485例患者研究队列上对MedDx进行基准测试，以基于病历审查的参考作为金标准。MedDx与金标准在三分类Cohen's {kappa}上的一致度为0.92，而AUD诊断代码为0.67。它在全部485份病历上与一位肝病专科医师的一致度为0.85，在186份病历上与第二位肝病专科医师的一致度为0.82，而两位肝病专科医师在这些病历上的一致度为0.87。按登记库加权后，其灵敏度为98%、特异度为94%，而AUD诊断代码为63%和96%；在估计的6,223例AUD患者中，61%在首次肝硬化诊断时没有AUD诊断。MedDx作为一款现成可用、公平且可审计的AUD识别工具公开可用。

title: TAT-Det: A Dataset for Testicular Appendage Torsion Detection and Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
zh_title: TAT-Det：超声睾丸附件扭转检测与分割数据集
summary: 预印本发布专家标注的小儿超声数据集 TAT-Det，含 2600 张图像、1203 例患者及检测与分割基准。
key_points: 2600 张超声图像，来自 1203 例患者
含病灶级框与像素级分割掩膜
多阶段标注流程并给出检测与分割基线
reason: 新公开标注数据集填补小儿急性阴囊急症空白，但为预印本、单中心，未见外部验证
abstract: Background: Testicular appendage torsion (TAT) is the leading cause of acute scrotal pain in prepubertal children. Yet, its diagnosis remains challenging due to nonspecific clinical manifestations and the absence of standardized datasets for pediatric acute scrotal emergencies. Results: We present TAT-Det, an expert-annotated ultrasound dataset specifically designed for TAT. TAT-Det comprises 2,600 ultrasound images from 1,203 patients collected at the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Each TAT-positive image is accompanied by lesion-level bounding boxes for detection and pixel-level segmentation masks for fine-grained delineation. Annotations were produced through a multi-stage workflow involving independent annotation by board-certified pediatric sonographers, consensus review, and refinement. Baseline benchmarks for object detection and semantic segmentation using representative deep learning models are further provided, with YOLO11m achieving the best detection performance and RWKV-UNet the best segmentation performance. Conclusions: TAT-Det addresses the lack of publicly available resources for pediatric emergency ultrasound and establishes a foundation for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence methods for automated TAT analysis.
zh_abstract: 【背景】睾丸附件扭转（TAT）是青春期前儿童急性阴囊疼痛的主要原因。然而，由于其临床表现非特异，且缺乏针对儿童急性阴囊急症的标准化数据集，其诊断仍然具有挑战性。【结果】我们提出TAT-Det，这是一个专为TAT设计的专家标注超声数据集。TAT-Det包含来自1203例患者的2600张超声图像，采集于浙江大学医学院附属儿童医院。每张TAT阳性图像均配有用于检测的病灶级边界框和用于细粒度勾画的像素级分割掩膜。标注通过多阶段工作流程产生，包括由委员会认证的儿科超声医师独立标注、共识审核和修订。进一步提供了使用代表性深度学习模型进行目标检测和语义分割的基线基准，其中YOLO11m取得了最佳检测性能，RWKV-UNet取得了最佳分割性能。【结论】TAT-Det解决了儿童急诊超声缺乏公开可用资源的问题，并为开发和评估用于自动化TAT分析的人工智能方法奠定了基础。

title: Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models Across the Heart Failure Care Pathway: A Narrative Review.
zh_title: 心衰诊疗路径中的AI与大语言模型：叙述性综述
summary: 叙述性综述评估 LLM 在心衰各诊疗环节的直接证据，并提出基于风险的临床评价与治理框架。
key_points: LLM 直接证据集中于病历抽取与文书撰写等任务
仅一项小型随机预试验涉及药物治疗优化
提出按任务成熟度分级的评价与治理框架
reason: 综述梳理证据成熟度并提出治理框架，但为叙述性综述，证据最高档位受限
abstract: [Journal of personalized medicine] Heart failure affects more than 64 million people worldwide and remains associated with high mortality and recurrent hospitalisation. Artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), is being evaluated across the care pathway, but evidence maturity varies by task. The aim of this narrative review was to appraise direct evidence for LLM applications in heart failure, distinguish it from supporting evidence for other AI methods and propose a risk-based framework for clinical evaluation and governance. The strongest direct LLM evidence concerns electronic health record extraction, document drafting, patient information and clinical trial endpoint adjudication. A small, randomised pilot evaluated supervised generative-AI-guided optimisation of guideline-directed medical therapy. Prospective case-finding and monitoring evidence largely concerns non-LLM AI. For conversational AI telemonitoring (a natural language interface with rule-based alerting), prospective evidence was limited to a single non-randomised controlled pilot. Performance depends on task definition, data completeness, human review and workflow adoption. Overall, LLMs can support clearly defined, supervised heart failure tasks, but current evidence does not justify autonomous high-stakes care. The evidence base is expanding but predominantly retrospective. Prospective trials, disease-specific benchmarks, equity assessment and regulatory engagement are prerequisites for safe clinical translation. Human oversight remains essential across all current-generation applications.
zh_abstract: [Journal of personalized medicine] 心力衰竭影响全球超过6400万人，并且仍与高死亡率和反复住院相关。人工智能（AI），包括大语言模型（LLMs），正在整个诊疗路径中接受评估，但证据成熟度因任务而异。本叙述性综述旨在评估LLM应用于心力衰竭的直接证据，将其与其他AI方法的支持性证据区分开，并提出一个用于临床评价与治理的基于风险的框架。最强的直接LLM证据涉及电子健康记录提取、文档起草、患者信息和临床试验终点裁定。一项小型随机试点评估了在监督下由生成式AI引导的指南指导药物治疗优化。前瞻性病例发现和监测证据主要涉及非LLM AI。对于对话式AI远程监测（一种具有基于规则警报的自然语言接口），前瞻性证据仅限于一项非随机对照试点。性能取决于任务定义、数据完整性、人工审核和工作流程采用。总体而言，LLMs可以支持定义明确、有监督的心力衰竭任务，但当前证据不足以证明可将其用于自主的高风险诊疗。证据基础正在扩大，但主要为回顾性证据。前瞻性试验、疾病特异性基准、公平性评估和监管参与是安全临床转化的前提。对于所有当前一代应用，人工监督仍然至关重要。

title: Biometric Monitoring and Machine Learning to Improve Preoperative Risk Stratification in Major Non-cardiac Surgery
zh_title: 可穿戴监测与机器学习改善非心脏大手术术前风险分层
summary: Sunnybrook 注册的一项 400 例介入性试验，拟用可穿戴生物监测与机器学习优化术前风险分层，尚未招募。
key_points: 注册为介入性试验，计划入组 400 例
以可穿戴设备数据结合机器学习预测术后并发症
当前状态为尚未开始招募，无结果
reason: 前瞻性设计是加分项，但仅为注册信息、无结果且样本量有限，属增量档
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre; conditions: Surgery, Postoperative Complications, Risk Assessment, Elective Surgical Procedure, Surgery-Complications; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 400; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Many patients undergoing surgery experience complications which can lead to reduced independence and quality of life. Prior to surgery, doctors attempt to anticipate the risk of complications using information about a patient's current health, lifestyle, and medical records. The more useful health information doctors have, the more accurately they can predict whether someone is likely to develop a complication. New technology, such as wearables (e.g., smartwatches), which are widely available and frequently used by the general public, can provide detailed health information outside of the immediate clinical environment, such as heart rate, steps taken/distance walked in a day, and sleep quality. The study is looking at whether the information from such a device could be used by doctors to more reliably predict who is likely to experience complications following surgery. The study will consist of two phases. The first phase (piloting) will examine practical difficulties in recruiting patients and having them wear the device. In the second phase, we will assess if the information provided by the wearable is indeed able to help predict which patients are most likely to develop complications after surgery. All participants in both phases of the study will be asked to wear the device for 48 hours in the 3 months before their scheduled surgery.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre；疾病/状况：手术、术后并发症、风险评估、择期手术、手术并发症；类型：干预性（INTERVENTIONAL）；分期：不适用（NA）；入组人数：400；状态：尚未招募（NOT_YET_RECRUITING）] 许多接受手术的患者会发生并发症，这可能导致独立性和生活质量下降。手术前，医生尝试利用患者当前健康状况、生活方式和医疗记录中的信息来预判并发症风险。医生拥有的有用健康信息越多，就越能准确预测某人是否可能发生并发症。可穿戴设备（例如智能手表）等新技术已广泛可用并被公众频繁使用，可在即时临床环境之外提供详细的健康信息，例如心率、每日步数/步行距离和睡眠质量。该研究正在考察此类设备提供的信息能否被医生用来更可靠地预测谁可能在手术后发生并发症。该研究将包括两个阶段。第一阶段（试点）将考察招募患者并让其佩戴设备方面的实际困难。在第二阶段，我们将评估可穿戴设备提供的信息是否确实能够帮助预测哪些患者最可能在手术后发生并发症。研究两个阶段的所有参与者都将被要求在预定手术前的3个月内佩戴该设备48小时。
